contexts.text: Gopher wood is a wood abounding in sulphur like the fir, and many others of its kind. It is from its sulphur that it is predicated of it that it signifies concupiscences, because it easily catches fire.
Fire, sulphur, and woods () = filthy cupidities.
Sulphur, bitumen, etc. in the Word, are predicated of cupidities, especially of those which are of the love of self.
Bitumen, being sulphureous and fiery...
Pitch and sulphur () = the falsities and evils of cupidities. AC 6724.
The whole land sulphur and salt, a burning () = goods and truths vastated; sulphur = the vastation of good. AC 2455:2.
Bitumen = cupidities, from the foul sulphureous stench in such water.
(Sulphur rained on Sodom) () = the Hell of those who are in the evils of the love of self... Sulphur = the Hell of the evils of the love of self. AC 2446, Illustrated.
There succeeded a yellow lumen as from sulphur. Described. AC 4418.
Because bitumen and pitch are sulphureous and black, they = evil and falsity.
Fire and sulphur () = the love of self and the derivative cupidities...
A river of sulphur () = falsities from the evils of the love of self and of the world.
Fire and sulphur () = the evils of the love of self and of the world.
In some cases the lumen (of the infernals) is like that from burning sulphur.

Having breastplates fiery, hyacinthine, and sulphureous () = their argumentations imaginary and visionary from infernal love and Own intelligence, and from the derivative concupiscences... By sulphur is signified the concupiscence from that love through Own intelligence. AR 452:2, Illustrated. AE 576.

Out of their mouth issued fire, and smoke, and sulphur () = that in their thoughts and discourse, regarded interiorly, there is nothing else, and from them proceeds nothing else, than the love of self and of the world, which is the proprium of the will; the conceit of Own intelligence, which is the proprium of the understanding; and the concupiscences of evil and falsity, which is the general proprium flowing forth from the two former. See AE 578.
And shall be tormented with fire and sulphur... () = the love of self and of the world, and the derivative cupidities... and the torment in Hell from them. See AE 888.

The lake of fire burning with sulphur () = the Hell where are the loves of falsity, and at the same time the cupidities of evil... Sulphur = the cupidity of evil and of the derivative falsity. AR 864. AR 893.
The Hell where such are appears at a distance like a fiery lake with a green flame as of sulphur. But they who are in it do not see this.
Like bottles filled with iron filings mixed with powdered sulphur, into which if water be poured there arises a heat... TCR 113. TCR 116:end.
(Hells in the west which appeared like lakes of fire and sulphur)... There appears as it were sulphur, from the love of what is false.
A fireplace into which the servants threw sulphurated and bituminous torches...
The ground was a mixture of sulphur, iron-filings, and clay. TCR 110:8.
The statues, being composed of a mixture of sulphur, iron-filings, and clay, began to bubble, as is the case with a mixture of these ingredients when water is poured upon it.
Like the light over sulphurated glebes in the night.
Like what takes place in swampy and sulphureous places in midwinter, after sunset: such a light, fatuous and cold, is often seen by travellers.
Like sulphureous stones thrown into the depths of the sea.
These are nocturnal lights, nay, waxen lights, rather, because there is in them more of sulphur...
They are then encompassed with sulphur and the derivative fire...
There was as it were the smoke of a furnace mixed with sulphureous fire.
Hells where there appears fire, as it were from what is sulphureous. SE 5096.
Lakes of sulphur. Explained. SE 5207.

Where the women dwelt there appeared a lucidity as it were sulphureous, which was from the lasciviousness in which they had been (here); for lasciviousness with women appears so (there) when they are together.
The women were cast into a place burning with sulphur and fire... DeConj 93.
Then all these women... were cast into the sulphureous lake...
There appears in the other life a rain of fire and sulphur, attended with a sense of combustion; and then the land where they are yawns asunder and becomes like a lake...

Of sulphur, or sulphureous = the concupiscence of destroying the goods and truths of the Church through the falsities of evil; here, = falsity burning from the loves of self and of the world. AE 578, Illustrated. AE 579.

As the falsities of evil from the love of self had destroyed them, it rained sulphur and fire (on Sodom); sulphur, from the concupiscence of destroying the Church through the falsities of evil... Such a rain appears in the Spiritual World also when the evil who are in falsities from that love are being cast down into Hell. AE 653:11.
By sulphur is meant such falsity of evil as destroys everything of the Church with man, which is the falsity from the evil of the love of self...
The evils of falsity and the falsities of evil are signified by fire and sulphur ().
By sulphur () is signified the vastation of all good through the concupiscences from evils. AE 653:13.
Sulphur = the love of falsity from evil, properly, the concupiscence of destroying the truths of good of the Church by means of the falsities of evil.
Snares, fire, and sulphur () = falsities and evils seducing.
